title: Sub-Doppler cooling of trapped ions using optical tweezers
authors: Bas Gerritsen, Liam J. Bond, Jiri Minář, Arghavan Safavi-Naini, Robert J. Spreeuw, Rene Gerritsma
abstract: We propose a sub-Doppler cooling scheme for trapped-ion crystals in Paul traps. The combination of a hollow tweezer and microwave drive creates an effective two-level system which is cooled through attractive Sisyphus cooling. For ${}^{171}\rm{Yb}^+$ ions, we numerically identify optimal parameters for one- and two-ion crystals, and investigate the cooling rate in ion crystals with up to three ions. Our cooling scheme utilizes a single ion addressed with a tweezer to achieve sub-Doppler cooling of the $N$ axial motional modes perpendicular to the tweezer propagation direction, does not rely on the Lamb-Dicke regime and uses off-resonant light. We reach $1/e$ cooling times for the center of mass mode of $τ_{\rm com}<2$ ms, and a steady-state excitation number of $\bar{n}_{\rm{com}}\approx 0.7$. Our scheme is well-suited as an intermediate stage between Doppler cooling and ground-state sideband cooling, and can be readily realized in trapped-ion platforms.
summary: This paper details a theoretical sub-Doppler cooling scheme for trapped-ion crystals using optical tweezers and microwave drives. By modeling the system as a three-level atom coupled to motional modes, the authors numerically demonstrate fast cooling rates for multiple ion chains. This method offers a versatile tool for preparing quantum states in trapped-ion quantum simulators.
main_problem: The paper proposes and investigates a novel sub-Doppler cooling scheme for trapped-ion crystals using optical tweezers.
main_result: The scheme achieves fast cooling rates, reaching $1/e$ cooling times below 2 ms for the center of mass mode, and is suitable as an intermediate cooling stage between Doppler and ground-state sideband cooling.
method: The dynamics are modeled using a three-level system and solved by numerically simulating the open quantum system evolution via the Lindblad master equation and quantum trajectories.
model_or_system: The physical system is trapped ions in Paul traps, cooled by a combination of a hollow optical tweezer and microwave drive. The internal states are modeled as a three-level system ($\{|gangle, |eangle, |aangle\}$) which is reduced to an effective two-level system for analysis.
key_observables: Cooling time ($	au$), steady-state excitation number ($ ar{n}_{	ext{com}}$), and the evolution of motional modes (center of mass, stretch).
important_parameters: Tweezer detunings ($\Delta_L$), Rabi frequencies ($\Omega$), and trapping frequencies ($\omega_P, \omega_T$).
main_assumptions: The scheme does not rely on the Lamb-Dicke regime and utilizes off-resonant light. The analysis often involves adiabatic elimination of auxiliary states.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the cooling mechanism (Sisyphus cooling) and show the time evolution of the center of mass mode occupation for one, two, and three ion crystals, comparing numerical results with variational ansatz predictions.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the cooling scheme and the underlying physics, develops the Hamiltonian and master equation, and then uses advanced numerical techniques (quantum trajectories, variational ansatz) to simulate and optimize the cooling parameters for various ion crystal sizes.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for implementing advanced cooling techniques in trapped ions, moving beyond standard Doppler cooling by leveraging engineered light-matter interactions in a controlled manner.
